claim: Diagnoses are exactly the minimal hitting sets of the minimal conflict sets; Reiter's and de Kleer-Williams' characterisations coincide. Parsimony means subset-minimal, not most probable.
schema_part: O (code-run hitting-set solver) / G on parsimony
agent_test: Give the agent a toy circuit puzzle set; compare LLM-only vs LLM that emits conflicts and a code-run hitting-set step; same token budget; score exact diagnosis set.

claim: The original HS-tree algorithm as printed was incorrect (counterexample {{a,b},{b,c},{a,c},{b,d},{b}}); a correction was published in 1989. Any solver used by the agent must follow the corrected version or be validated against brute force.
agent_test: Cross-check the agent's solver against brute-force enumeration on random conflict collections.

claim: Exact diagnosis does not scale on large circuits: complete algorithms (CDA, HA) solved 0-12% of c880/c1908 observations in 1 min while anytime stochastic SAFARI solved 100% on all 14 circuits, without minimality guarantee.
agent_test: Run solver with time cap; compare exact vs anytime on growing problem sizes.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Analysing failing observations one at a time breaks down; aggregating all observations in one formulation scales (1140/1140 solved vs 177-185 enumerated with LBX/RS; CFaults 31-36% more programs than BugAssist/SNIPER).
agent_test: In multi-failure tasks, test pooling all failing cases in one conflict step vs per-case diagnosis.

claim: Entropy / expected-information probe selection beats split-in-half and random in query-based debugging (over 50% fewer queries at diagnosis cardinality 2), but depends on prior fault probabilities and on sampling; best-first samples were biased yet gave the fewest measurements. Prior-quality robustness: with a bad prior entropy lost at most about one query on short sessions and won beyond 10 queries (d12).
agent_test: Compare agent probe choice: LLM free choice vs code-computed entropy over candidate set at equal token count.

claim: Active testing shrinks the remaining candidate set roughly geometrically (average decay p=0.7, R2=0.88) with greedy test choice.
agent_test: Log candidate-set size per test and fit decay.

claim: Repair guided by solver-derived conflicts is far safer than LLM self-diagnosis: LLM-diagnostic repair broke 11.8% of correct artifacts vs 1.3% for conflict-based DRAGO. Task-independent: plain self-revision without an oracle also lowered accuracy in GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 and GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 (d05).
agent_test: Replicate regression-rate comparison on our own code/spec tasks.

claim: LLM self-repair is bottlenecked by the quality of the diagnosis: GPT-4 feedback 33.30% vs human feedback 52.60% repair success (verified in source).
agent_test: Hold repairer fixed; vary diagnosis source (self, code-run, oracle) at equal tokens.

claim: Real execution feedback matters; imagined tool output hurts: AutoSD with real debugger 73% plausible vs 63% ablated.
agent_test: Ablate real vs model-simulated tool output.

claim: LLM stated confidence is a weak trust signal in fault localisation: confidence>=0.9 on 76.2% of answers, only 84.1% correct; a structured scaffold gave no accuracy gain over the same inputs (81.4 vs 82.0) but made answers checkable. Verbalised confidence is overconfident (GPT-4 average failure-prediction AUROC 62.7%, d10), though calibration is good when a model scores explicit options (d11).
agent_test: Measure calibration of agent confidence vs code-verified result.

claim: LLM agents are poor at choosing what information to request next: best of 32 models 68%, information use fell from 57% to 26% in the last round; fluent reasoning (91% above rubric) did not predict accuracy. Independent: QuestBench found models at 40-50% on Logic-Q and Planning-Q; explicit information-gain selection raised success by 38.1% (UoT) and 37.4 points (BED-LLM) over direct prompting.
agent_test: Replace LLM probe choice with entropy rule on a clinical or device task; compare.

claim: LLM agents on live cloud-fault diagnosis are inconsistent: acc@1 localisation 61.54% best (GPT-4 w/ shell), RCA 45.45% best; accuracy saturates after a few steps when feedback is only environment output.
agent_test: Use AIOpsLab subset with and without an explicit structural model.

claim: A model-derived procedure can diagnose network faults quickly: 100% of injected faults; real cloud faults 30 of 33 (3 intermittent counted as failures), only 8 fault classes were actually injected; humans 14:44-33:48 min vs NetDx 1:38 min.
agent_test: Not directly; need a domain model for our tasks.

claim: Using an LLM to translate and a classical reasoner to reason (foundation theory of 128 rules, 97.4% agreement, 92% reuse) beats LLM-only reasoning on hard incidents, but is preprint-only.
schema_part: O (LLM as translator, code as reasoner)
agent_test: Compare LLM-only vs LLM-writes-model + solver on a rule-based diagnosis set.

claim: Accurate fault locations cut LLM repair tokens by up to 39.2%, but many FL methods cost more than they save.
agent_test: Token-ledger of localise-then-repair vs direct repair.

claim: Repeated runs and agreement raise localisation accuracy and give a confidence hint, but samples from one model are correlated.
agent_test: Check agreement vs correctness across seeds.

claim: The consistency-based theory needs a correct behavioural model; with a wrong model the diagnosis can be wrong or empty, and weak-fault models give many candidates (up to 450 minimal candidates). LLM-built models are error-prone: GPT-4 PDDL models had 2 to 53 errors per domain and only 25% of valid domains matched the reference behaviour (d06, d07).
agent_test: Inject a wrong model and measure harm.

claim: No single reasoner wins across domains: junction tree solved 23/129 power-network instances but most of the software-process set.
agent_test: Benchmark solver choice by instance features.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: No study tests a code-run conflict and hitting-set step added to an LLM agent against LLM-only diagnosis at equal tokens on circuits or rule bases. Indirect evidence: LLMs doing the GDE steps themselves reach F1 0.917 (conflicts) and 0.784 (diagnoses) with accuracy falling as diagnosis count grows, and solver-backed LLM pipelines beat LLM-only on 4 of 5 logic sets (Logic-LM, GPT-4 avg +39.2% over standard, +18.4% over CoT) but lose where CoT is strong (PrOntoQA 98.79 CoT vs 83.20).
schema_part: O (code-run reasoner), G (ground in code output)
agent_test: Run LLM-only vs LLM+hitting-set at equal tokens on a generated circuit set, per task type.

claim: Information-gain question or probe choice beats LLM-chosen next questions by a large margin when the hypothesis set is explicit: +38.1% (UoT, average across LLMs; FloDial troubleshooting 42.5 to 67.8 GPT-4) and +37.4 points (BED-LLM, 20 Questions). Both used LLM-simulated probabilities, not a code-computed model, so the gain from fully code-computed entropy is untested.
agent_test: Compare LLM-picked probes, LLM-simulated EIG and code EIG on one fault set.

claim: A strong LLM can draft a system model but it is not trustworthy unchecked: GPT-4 PDDL models had 53, 2 and 4 errors in the three domains, GPT-3.5 over 350; LLaMA-2-70b gave valid PDDL in 94% of domains but only 25% behaviourally matched the reference. With validator feedback GPT-4 fixed all 56 factual errors (3 corrections added new errors). How a 5-10% wrong model changes diagnoses was not measured by any source found.
agent_test: Inject 5-10% wrong rules in a circuit model and measure harm to top-1 diagnosis.

claim: The adversarial check on LLM-written models works in one preprint: disabling the counterexample step dropped agreement with ground truth from 97.4% to 41%, and 48 of 50 planted wrong rules were caught (TypoNet).
agent_test: Repeat on a second domain.

claim: LLM self-revision regresses on correct answers across task types: 11.8% of correct specifications broken (DRAGO study), GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1, GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 without oracle labels. Whether conflict-based gating transfers beyond specifications and PDDL is untested.
agent_test: Gate edits on a code check in a new domain and compare the break rate.

claim: Exact diagnosis fails at modest size while anytime and SAT-based methods keep working: CDA/HA solved 0-12% of c880/c1908 in 1 minute, SAFARI 100% (no minimality guarantee); implicit-hitting-set with MaxSAT solved 1140/1140 multi-observation instances. For a token-limited agent: use an anytime or SAT-based call with a time cap, and report non-minimal results as such. NP-hardness of abduction (Bylander 1991) is secondary-sourced only.
agent_test: Time exact vs anytime vs MaxSAT on generated circuits by size.

claim: Intermittent faults cost far more observations than persistent ones (ISCAS85: 2.7-5.5 persistent vs 29-126 intermittent at g=0.9), and need a second number per part (chance it works when faulted). Several simultaneous faults are handled by the GDE framework but LLM diagnosis enumeration decays with diagnosis count (F1 0.784 for o3-mini). The NetDx study treated intermittent faults as failures.
agent_test: Test a single pass vs repeated probes on injected intermittent faults.

claim: Oracle errors: the interactive algorithm assumes the answerer never errs and cannot detect a wrong answer. No study measured LLM oracle error on probe queries or diagnosis robustness to wrong answers; the human figure (a quarter of users erring at least once) is the only number. An empty candidate set after a contradiction is the cheap signal.
agent_test: Simulate a wrong-answer rate on probe responses and measure the recovery rate.

claim: Stated LLM confidence is a poor fault prior: verbalised confidence clusters at 80-100%, GPT-4 failure-prediction AUROC 62.7% (close to chance), LLM-sampled hypotheses collapse onto a few modes (Van Gogh 93 of 200). Entropy selection tolerates a bad prior (at most about one extra query in short sessions; better beyond 10 queries), so a flat or structure-based prior is the safe default.
agent_test: Compare uniform, LLM-confidence and sample-agreement priors on query counts.
